fields.hero_description: Build a dermaplaning consent form in your practice's wording that clients sign by link and that files each signature by client.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Carries Into the Treatment Room
fields.features_subheading: Your provider or lawyer writes the consent text. Emergent builds the form, and the app files each signature on the client's record.
fields.feature_1:
Statements initialed one at a time

Paste the consent wording your provider or lawyer approved. The form splits it into numbered statements with an initials box each, and the client signs once every box is filled.
fields.feature_2:
Skin history in your own questions

Write the skin history questions your practice asks, word for word. A yes to any one of them marks the booking for review, and the answers stay on the client's record in the app.
fields.feature_3:
Alerts that carry a link, not answers

Send the esthetician an email or a Slack message when a form needs review. The alert names the booking and links to the form. Health answers never sit in an inbox or a channel.
fields.feature_4:
A signature on every record

Clients sign with a finger or a mouse at the end of the form. The app saves the signature with the date, the time, and the version of the consent wording the client read first.
fields.feature_5:
A fresh link after 12 months

Set how long a signed form stays current. When a returning client last signed more than 12 months ago, the app emails a new signing link along with the booking confirmation.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, in your GitHub

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and host the form next to your booking system. Keep building on it there, or keep changing it by prompting Emergent.

fields.tab_content_1:
Jovana's add-on puts 4 statements into her facial form

Jovana Enright books a hydrating facial at Velvetleaf Skin Studio, then adds dermaplaning before she pays. Her consent link opens the facial terms plus 4 dermaplaning statements to initial. A client who books the facial alone never sees them. Jovana signs once, and her record reads facial and dermaplaning signed.
fields.tab_content_2:
All 5 Saturday clients signed before Ingrith loads the car

Ingrith Ivanska works out of her car as Glowcart Mobile Facials, with no front desk and no clipboard. Each booking confirmation email carries the consent link. On Saturday morning her schedule shows 5 dermaplaning appointments and 5 signed forms, each next to the client's address and start time.
fields.tab_content_3:
After one yes, Tullia's booking waits for Desmonda

Tullia Kestrova answers yes to 1 of the skin history questions Gildenrow Aesthetics wrote. Her Thursday booking is marked needs review. Desmonda Rosewarne, the esthetician, gets an email that a form needs review, with a link to open it. The answer stays in the app, and Desmonda reads it there before she confirms.
fields.tab_content_4:
By Friday, Ragnhild has countersigned 11 of 12

Every student treatment on the Treharne School of Esthetics clinic floor carries 2 signatures: the client's and the instructor's. Student Birgitta adds her name to each form, and instructor Ragnhild countersigns from her tablet. By Friday, 11 of this week's 12 are countersigned, and 1 waits on her list.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Dermaplaning Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a dermaplaning consent form in your own approved wording that clients sign online before treatment.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Gather the forms you use now
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write your own skin history questions
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Name who opens a held form
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull together the paper consent, the intake sheet, and any aftercare handout you give dermaplaning clients today. Note which pages clients sign and which they only read. That split decides what becomes a statement to initial and what stays as plain text.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Have the provider your practice works with, or a lawyer, approve the consent text before it goes into the form. Record the date of each approved version. Every signed record then points to the exact wording that client read.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each skin history question the way your practice asks it, with a yes or no answer and a box for details. Then decide which answers hold a booking for review. Your provider makes those calls, not the form.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the esthetician or manager who reads a form after a client answers yes. Their email carries the booking and a link, never the answers. For a student clinic, also name the instructor who countersigns each treatment.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the approved wording and your questions into a prompt, then say when the dermaplaning section opens, for example only when it is added to a facial. Emergent builds the form and its database, and you change either by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Put the link in every booking
fields.howto_step_6_des: Add the signing link to your booking confirmation email. Set how long a signature stays current, such as 12 months. A returning client past that point gets a fresh link with the next confirmation instead of signing at the door.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit the form twice: once for a facial alone and once for a facial with dermaplaning where you answer yes to one skin history question. Check that the add-on statements show only on the second, and that the held booking email has no answers in it.

faq_plan.q: What is a dermaplaning consent form?
faq_plan.a: A dermaplaning consent form is the document a client reads and signs before a dermaplaning treatment, agreeing to it as your practice describes it. MedlinePlus explains written informed consent in the same terms: "Then you will read a description of it and sign a form." Your provider or lawyer decides what that description says.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a dermaplaning consent form?
faq_plan.a: Paste your approved consent wording and your skin history questions into Emergent's AI form builder, and say who reviews a form when a client answers yes. Emergent builds the fields, the review rule, and the database from that prompt. Run one sample booking through it before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What sections should a dermaplaning consent form have?
faq_plan.a: Build it in this order: client details, a description of the treatment in your practice's words, your skin history questions, aftercare terms, an optional photo release, and the signature with the date. Give each consent statement its own initials box. Your provider or lawyer approves the wording in every section.

faq_plan.q: Can a dermaplaning consent form also cover brow waxing?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put the dermaplaning statements and a brow waxing section in one form, and open each section only when that service is on the booking. To keep them apart, a separate waxing consent form can sit on the same client record.

faq_plan.q: Can clients re-sign a dermaplaning consent form every year?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Choose a renewal period, and the app emails a fresh signing link with the booking confirmation once that period has passed. Each signature is saved as its own record with the date and the wording version. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and earlier signatures stay on file.

faq_plan.q: Can clients sign a dermaplaning consent form on their phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The link opens in any phone browser, and the client initials each statement and signs with a finger. The record shows when they signed. Whether an electronic signature meets the rules where you practice is a question for your lawyer. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: Can a dermaplaning consent form ask first-time clients different questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask whether this is the client's first dermaplaning visit, and show extra questions only after a yes, such as which products they use at home. Returning clients go straight to the statements. Put that rule in your prompt, and the form follows it.

faq_plan.q: Where do skin history answers go after a client signs a dermaplaning consent form?
faq_plan.a: They are saved on the client's record, next to the signature, in a database you own. An alert about a held booking carries a link to the form and leaves the answers out. Decide who may open those records.

faq_plan.q: Can I add a photo release to a dermaplaning consent form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add before-and-after photo permission as its own checkbox, apart from the treatment consent. A client can then agree to the treatment and still decline photos. The app saves that choice on the client's record, and you can filter for clients who said yes before posting anything.

faq_plan.q: Can I adapt another consent form for dermaplaning?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Paste the text of a form you already use, such as a lash or tattoo consent form, then say in your prompt what changes for dermaplaning. Have your provider or lawyer approve the dermaplaning wording before any client signs it.

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable dermaplaning consent PDFs and fill-and-sign templates (spa practice forms, a forms bundle, PDF editors, two form-builder templates): one sheet, signed once, filed. This page shows the form as an app a skin practice runs: a dermaplaning section that opens only when a client adds it to a facial, links signed before a mobile esthetician leaves home, a skin history yes that holds the booking for review without sending the answers in the alert, and student treatments countersigned by the instructor. The consent wording stays with the practice's provider or lawyer; the page makes no claim about dermaplaning risks, contraindications, who may perform it or whether a signature makes consent valid, and quotes MedlinePlus only for what written informed consent is.
